claims.reason: The instance comes from `variable [AddLeftMono α]` in section Cov. The theorem includes it because it is instance-implicit and its type mentions only α, but nothing in the statement `a + c - (b + c) ≤ a - b` needs it to elaborate. The argument that `OrderedSub` gives monotonicity checks out. `add_tsub_le_right` (line 68, needs only Preorder/Add/Sub/OrderedSub) gives x + c - c ≤ x. If x ≤ y, transitivity gives x + c - c ≤ y. Then `tsub_le_iff_right` (a - b ≤ c ↔ a ≤ c + b, the field of `OrderedSub`) turns this into x + c ≤ y + c. Proof without the instance: by `tsub_le_iff_left` (line 91, needs no monotonicity) the goal becomes a + c ≤ b + c + (a - b). `le_add_tsub` (line 93) gives a ≤ b + (a - b). Monotonicity as above gives a + c ≤ b + (a - b) + c. That equals b + c + (a - b) by `add_right_comm`. Every lemma used is stated before `section Cov` without `AddLeftMono`, and the argument has no gap, so the hypothesis can be deleted.
